question: A merchant fixes the marked price of his goods at 50% above the cost price. He sells his goods at 12% discount. His percentage of profit is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The successive percentage formula can be directly used to find the net profit percentage.

Net Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 50 − 12 − (50 × 12) ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 38 − 600 ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 38 − 6 = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = 100
 
 
 MP = 150
 
 
 SP = 132
 
 

 +50% Markup
 
 

 −12% Discount
 
 

 +32% Profit
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Given:**

Markup percentage = 50% above CP

Discount percentage = 12% on MP

**Formulas Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Markup %) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150

⇒ Discount = 12% of MP

⇒ Discount = (12 ÷ 100) × 150 = 18

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 150 − 18 = 132

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 132 − 100 = 32

⇒ Profit % = (32 ÷ 100) × 100 = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed or tagged on an article is called its marked price. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price or Selling Price.

Relation between CP and MP

A direct relationship ratio between CP and MP is: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount %) ÷ (100 + Profit %).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.
